	<ResortReportHeadline>The Calm Before the Storm!</ResortReportHeadline>
	<ResortReport><p>It looks like a glorious day on the way.&nbsp; The sky is full of stars and there is just a light breeze from the west, which is forecast to swing to the north and increase a little during the day.&nbsp; The current temperature is just below zero and we are heading for a very pleasant top of 5 degrees.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p><p>The snow has had a decent freeze overnight, but it feels like there will be enough texture on the surface for firm but good turns on the groomers from the get-go.&nbsp; Sunny aspects should soften for nice spring-like turns as the day warms but shaded and south facing slopes will likely stay pretty firm and slick for the day.&nbsp; Follow the sun for fun turns all day.&nbsp;</p><p>Heavenly Valley area is not perfect but there will be plenty of fun turns to be had for advanced and expert skiers and riders.&nbsp; Just take notice of the signage, as some zones runs are upgraded, or may be closed if it's too slick.&nbsp; &nbsp;The Extreme Area remains closed due to a significant sliding hazard and please don't attempt to retrieve dropped equipment from any closed areas.</p><p>Get out there and make the most of the great weather and fun snow conditions today, as it looks like we have some real mountain weather on the way tomorrow, and we should be waking up to a much whiter mountain on Wednesday morning.&nbsp; Stay tuned!</p><p>Cheers Bill.&nbsp;</p></ResortReport>

	<Backcountry>27 July 2026

There is a significant sliding hazard in the backcountry again today, and all aspects will be firm and slick this morning.  Solar aspects may soften for spring-like turns as the day warms but shaded and south facing slopes will likely stay icy for the day.  The cover is ok at higher elevations but gets very thin and marginal the lower you go.  Take Care. </Backcountry>
